CHAR_F32S

Char-sheet stride — mirrors rust/text-draw's CHAR_F32S.

ATLAS_PAD_EM

Glyph overflow pad (fraction of font-size) — keeps descenders and the 0.12em rise inside the atlas cell.

(module scope)

Kind-specific wasm surface for the text-draw crate — typed on top of the generic WasmWidget so calls stay checked.

upload_atlas

Rasterized glyph strip — one cell per char, white-on-transparent.

set_chars

The 12-f32-per-char storage sheet (see file doc).

set_ink

The block's text color.

trigger

Anchors the stagger clock — frame() reports elapsed ms from here.

tryGpuDraw

tryGpuDraw — attempts the WebGPU reveal for a just-triggered element. Called from startAnimation after the char spans mount; resolves silently — on any failure the CSS animation is the render path (the canvas/class are only applied once the atlas + sheet are live).

  • @param host The draw-text element.
  • @param totalMs Wall-clock span of the reveal (last delay + duration)

(module scope)

prepare — measures the char spans, rasterizes the atlas, and pushes ink + sheet into the widget. Returns false when nothing measurable exists (hidden block, zero-size chars — the CSS path then stays authoritative).

  • @param host The draw-text element.
  • @param mounted Live widget handle.
  • @param contentEl The .draw-text content span.
  • @param chars The per-char spans.
  • @param canvas The overlay canvas.
  • @returns True when the widget is armed and triggered.

COPY_PITCH

bytesPerRow alignment required by copyTextureToBuffer.

BUFFER_COPY_DST

WebGPU usage/map-mode flag values — the DOM lib types these as plain numbers (GPUBufferUsageFlags/GPUMapModeFlags); the global GPUBufferUsage/GPUMapMode constant objects only exist on WebGPU runtimes, so the spec values are declared here instead of touching globalThis (which also keeps the happy-dom tests free of globals).

VERIFY_MAX_COVERAGE

Coverage ceiling for verifyOverlay — a glyph block's ink fills a small fraction of its box; a painted-coverage ratio at/above this means the draw degenerated into a full-bleed fill (the slab), and zero means it produced nothing (missing text).

(module scope)

verifyOverlay — arms-check for the GPU path: submits one frame at the reveal's end state (every char drawn) against the detached canvas, reads the painted texture back through the shared device, and accepts the overlay only when the coverage sits inside the glyph-block envelope (nonzero, non-full-bleed). Runs once per trigger — the readback is a single mapAsync, never on the frame path. Returns false on any readback/validation failure so the DOM reveal remains the render path.

  • @param mounted Live widget handle.
  • @param canvas The (not-yet-attached) overlay canvas.
  • @param probeMs ms past the last char's end — forces full reveal.
  • @returns True when the probe painted a plausible glyph block.

totalMsForProbe

totalMsForProbe — the probe's end-state timestamp: the last scheduled char's delay + its own duration, the point where every glyph is fully drawn. Kept separate from the wall-clock totalMs (which adds presentation slack) so the probe measures the real "all revealed" moment.

  • @param host The draw-text element.
  • @param chars The per-char spans.
  • @returns ms after the reveal's start where all chars are drawn.

drive

drive — the MANUAL rAF clock: advances the widget until the last char lands (or the element tears down), then drops the overlay. The DOM spans animate in parallel, so finish() is a same-state swap. The DOM-suppression class lands on the first submitted frame — the class flip and the canvas's first present composite together, so no frame ever shows neither paint source (the mount blink).

  • @param host The draw-text element.
  • @param mounted Live widget handle.
  • @param totalMs Reveal span — the overlay disarms after it.
  • @param contentEl The .draw-text content span — receives the

finish

finish — the end-state swap: drop the suppression class (the DOM chars' CSS animation already completed to the same rest state), then remove the canvas + widget.

  • @param host The draw-text element.

teardownGpuDraw

teardownGpuDraw — disarms the overlay without touching DOM paint: used by reset()/disconnectedCallback (where the DOM re-renders to the pending state on its own) and by finish (after the class drop).

  • @param host The draw-text element.
